frame_spacing.scaling_and_reasoning: Ford reuses the Nimitz hull form. Frame numbering runs from Frame 0 to Frame 265 over 1,060 ft length between perpendiculars/extremes (265 frames * 4 ft = 1,060 ft, matching Nimitz 4-ft frame spacing proven in NAWCWD TP 8475 p. 5 and CV-67 BOGP Sheet 1).

hangar_bay_count.citation: USS Gerald R. Ford (CVN 78) Fact Booklet, DVIDS, p. 7; corroborated by DVIDS News 414252 (2022 Inspection)

location_frame.scaling_and_reasoning: Ford consolidated the three Nimitz bays into two larger bays by eliminating one division door, positioning the single division door between forward Bay 1 and aft Bay 2 near mid-hangar (Nimitz had doors at Frame 128 and Frame 180).

hangar_clear_height.scaling_and_reasoning: Nimitz-class and prior supercarriers standard clear overhead is 25 ft (7.62 m) to accommodate carrier aircraft (F/A-18E/F, E-2D, MH-60) vertical maintenance envelopes.
hangar_clear_height.citation: NAWCWD TP 8516 / DTIC ADA432176 p. 18; NAWCWD TP 8475 p. 5

hangar_clear_width.scaling_and_reasoning: Direct inheritance of the Nimitz hull mold line at Main Deck level.
hangar_clear_width.citation: NAWCWD TP 8475 p. 5; Friedman U.S. Aircraft Carriers p. 320

hangar_length.scaling_and_reasoning: Spans Frame 64 to Frame 235 (171 frames * 4 ft = 684 ft = 208.5 m), identical longitudinal boundaries to Nimitz Main Deck hangar enclosure.

aircraft_elevator_count.citation: USS Gerald R. Ford (CVN 78) Fact Booklet, DVIDS, p. 4; HII Release 2013

elevator_1.position_description: Starboard forward of island, servicing Hangar Bay 1

frame_range.scaling_and_reasoning: Positions matching starboard forward elevator 1 on Nimitz and Kitty Hawk/JFK (CV-67 BOGP Sheet 4 Plate 7).

elevator_2.position_description: Starboard aft of island, servicing Hangar Bay 2

frame_range.scaling_and_reasoning: Matches starboard aft elevator position on Nimitz and CV-67 (CV-67 BOGP Sheet 4 Plate 7), shifted aft corresponding to Ford's smaller, aft-positioned island.

platform_dimensions.citation: Huntington Ingalls Industries Photo Release, 'Final Aircraft Elevator Installed on Gerald R. Ford (CVN 78)', Jan 2013

frame_range.scaling_and_reasoning: Matches port aft elevator position on Nimitz (El 4) and CV-67 (El 4) clear of the landing area foul line.

flight_deck_04.scaling_and_reasoning: Directly matches CV-67 / Kitty Hawk 04 Level moulded elevation of 97'-4" above baseline (BOGP Sheet 4 Plate 7), providing ~60 ft freeboard above 36'-8" design draft (NAWCWD TP 8516 p. 7: 'height of flight deck above waterline is about 60 feet').

gallery_deck_03.scaling_and_reasoning: Matches CV-67 03 Level moulded elevation of 87'-4" above baseline (BOGP Sheet 5 Plate 8).

weapons_handling_02.scaling_and_reasoning: Matches CV-67 02 Level moulded elevation of 78'-6" above baseline (BOGP Sheet 6 Plate 9).

gallery_intermediate_01.scaling_and_reasoning: Matches CV-67 01 Level moulded elevation of 69'-6" above baseline (BOGP Sheet 7 Plate 10).

main_deck_1.scaling_and_reasoning: Matches CV-67 / CVA-63 Main Deck (Hangar Floor) moulded elevation of 60'-10" above baseline (BOGP Sheet 8 Plate 11).

second_deck_2.scaling_and_reasoning: Matches CV-67 Second Deck moulded elevation of 51'-0" above baseline (9'-10" deck height below Main Deck).

third_deck_3.scaling_and_reasoning: Matches CV-67 Third Deck moulded elevation of 42'-5" above baseline (8'-7" deck height below Second Deck).

fourth_deck_4.scaling_and_reasoning: Matches CV-67 Fourth Deck moulded elevation of 33'-10" above baseline (8'-7" deck height below Third Deck).

first_platform.scaling_and_reasoning: Matches CV-67 First Platform moulded elevation of 24'-6" above baseline (9'-4" height below Fourth Deck).

second_platform.scaling_and_reasoning: Matches CV-67 Second Platform moulded elevation of 14'-0" above baseline (10'-6" height below First Platform).

inner_bottom.scaling_and_reasoning: Standard US Navy aircraft carrier double bottom depth of 5 ft above baseline keel.

baseline.citation: Standard naval architectural datum (bottom of flat plate keel)

transverse_bulkheads.scaling_and_reasoning: Because Ford reuses the Nimitz hull form and 4-ft frame grid, major transverse watertight bulkheads follow standard 16-frame (64 ft) machinery compartment intervals and 8-frame (32 ft) forward/aft subdivision intervals.
